content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates prices in the first 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, then gradually converges toward true values — suggesting a lag in adjusting to recent trends.
- After a sharp price spike, model forecasts overshoot and remain elevated longer than true values, indicating failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), particularly when true values show upward momentum.
- Forecasts tend to be overly optimistic in the first 3–5 days, then become more conservative — suggesting a delayed reaction to recent price movements.
- Model fails to account for short-term volatility clustering; forecasts smooth out sharp drops or spikes too aggressively.
- When true values show strong downward momentum, model forecasts remain stubbornly high — indicating a failure to recognize trend reversal.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 7–15 day window.
- Forecasts often lag behind true values by 1–3 days, particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon.
- Model exhibits a tendency to overfit recent high values, leading to persistent overestimation when true values are trending downward.
